27672.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
Coordinate and supervise the safe and efficient construction, installation, maintenance, and operation of underground infrastructure systems supporting mine production activities. This includes mine water supply systems, dewatering networks, power distribution, communications infrastructure, ventilation services, and associated underground projects.
The role provides day-to-day leadership, and supervision to project crews and operators, ensuring all work is completed in accordance with safety requirements, company standards, engineering specifications, and project schedules.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Supervising underground mine projects crews to ensure work is completed safely, efficiently, and to required quality standards.
Coordinating daily activities for infrastructure installation and maintenance projects.
Allocating personnel, equipment, and resources to achieve planned work schedules.
Monitoring work progress and provide regular updates to the Mine Projects Superintendent, Coordinators and Project Engineers.
Ensuring all infrastructure installations are completed in accordance with approved designs, procedures, and engineering specifications.
Leading pre-start meetings and communicate daily work priorities to crews.
Providing coaching, mentoring, and on-the-job training to operators and trades personnel.
Knowledge of weekly and daily planning requirements.
Coordinating infrastructure activities to minimise disruption to mining operations.
Maintaining accurate records of completed works, labour utilisation, equipment uses, and project progress.
Assisting with preparation of material requirements and resource forecasts.
Ensuring crews understand work plans, priorities, and operational requirements.
Promoting and demonstrating a strong safety culture at all times embracing K92’s CARES values.
Ensuring compliance with all site safety procedures, standards, and legislative requirements.
Conducting workplace inspections and participating in risk assessments.
Leading hazard identification, reporting, and implementing corrective action processes.
Investigating incidents and near misses and participating in root cause analysis activities.
Ensuring good housekeeping standards are maintained within all work areas.
Stopping work immediately where unsafe conditions or practices exist.
About You
To be considered for this role, you will have some or all the following.
Year 10 Certificate, Carpentry Trades certification or related.
PNG National Driver’s License (desirable).
Ability to interpret engineering designs and drawing and implement to best practices and standards.
Behaviour consistent with K92 Mining’s Values.
Ability to plan, coordinate, and supervise multiple work activities.
Good understanding of Mining or Civil infrastructure systems.
Exposure to mine infrastructure construction and installation projects (Desirable).
Eight plus (8+) Mining / Construction experience and two plus (2+) years’ appropriate experience in a similar role.
Sound knowledge of safe mining and construction practices and standards.
Proven multitasking skills and can work under extreme pressure.
Good analytical and teamwork skills.
Good written and verbal communication skills as well as good organizational, administrative and multitasking skills.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

27670.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
Assist the Senior Mine Control Operator coordinate and optimize the real-time dispatch of mining equipment and personnel to ensure efficient and safe operations. This involves monitoring fleet activity, analysing operational data, and using dispatch software to support production targets and minimize downtime.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Effectively administering the computerised mine dispatch system including management of disk space, system set-up parameters and back-up of daily data to optimise all functions of the system.
Effectively operating and maintaining the mine dispatch system to ensure that all elements are working correctly including reporting and communications functions.
Identifying trends, problems, inefficiencies or non-compliances with operating procedures, taking action or making recommendations for continuous improvement through reports and weekly system improvement meetings.
Providing materials movement, equipment utilisation and other production data to production planning or projects personnel on a daily, weekly or monthly basis or as otherwise required.
Ensuring effective processes for communicating relevant information, including company, site, department, and team performance, to all team members are in place.
Actively promoting a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrating personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
About You
To be considered for this role, you will have some or all the following.
Year 12 Certificate or diploma in Mining, Engineering, IT or related field
Behaviour consistent with K92 Mining’s Values.
Strong computer skills and exposure to mine dispatch systems.
Mining operational experience and three plus (3+) years’ appropriate experience in a similar role.
Sound knowledge of safe mining practices and standards in an underground mine.
Proven multitasking skills and can work under extreme pressure.
Good analytical and teamwork skills.
Good written and verbal communication skills as well as good organizational, administrative and multitasking skills.

Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. MAINTENANCE PLANNER
Job Purpose:
To plan, coordinate, and schedule all daily maintenance activities within the mill, ensuring resources, manpower, materials, and equipment are effectively allocated to achieve safe, timely, and efficient maintenance execution while minimizing operational downtime.
Main Responsibilities:
Laise with maintenance team to plan and schedule all maintenance work using SAP.

Strong understanding of mill equipment and maintenance practices, including pumps, motors, gearboxes, conveyors, boilers, turbines, sterilizers, presses, and utilities systems, with knowledge of preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance principles.

28032.description:
Technician – Underground Ventilations (241480)
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
NPL now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mine Technical Services Department as a
Technician – Underground Ventilations (241480)
.
About the role
Reporting to the Senior Drill and Blast Engineer, the Underground Ventilation Technician supports the planning, monitoring, and optimization of the underground mine ventilation system to ensure a safe, compliant, and productive working environment. The role involves conducting ventilation surveys, collecting and analyzing data, maintaining monitoring equipment, and assisting with ventilation planning and regulatory compliance.
In this role, you will:
•    Conduct routine underground ventilation surveys, including airflow, pressure, gas, temperature, humidity, and dust measurements.
•    Inspect ventilation controls such as stoppings, regulators, doors, seals, and ventilation fans.
•    Verify that ventilation circuits operate according to approved ventilation
•    Collect, record, and maintain accurate ventilation monitoring data.
•    Prepare routine ventilation reports and trend analyses.
•    Assist in updating ventilation models and mine ventilation plans.
•    Support investigations into ventilation-related incidents or abnormalities.
•    Assist ventilation engineers with short- and long-term ventilation planning.
•    Support the implementation of ventilation changes associated with mining development.
•    Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with the NPL Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health and safety rules and procedures
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
•    Bachelor’s degree in mining engineering, or a related discipline (preferred).
•    Underground mining induction and relevant site competencies.
•    Experience working in an underground mining environment.
•    Knowledge of underground ventilation principles.
•    Ability to use ventilation monitoring equipment.
•    Strong attention to detail and accurate record keeping.
•    Good communication and teamwork skills.
•    Computer literacy, including Microsoft Office and experience using ventilation software (e.g., Ventsim)
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately.

oin Our Team as a Technician – Underground Ventilations (241480)
Embark on a rewarding career with NPL as a Technician – Underground Ventilation. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.
Note:
This advert will be open until
15th August 2026
. If you do not hear from NPL within next two (2) weeks following the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity.

Very good customer service

27909.description:
Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Manager
Position Description
BACKGROUND
Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organization, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 120 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection.
Save the Children in Papua New Guinea (SCiPNG) is committed to be a platform for transformative and lasting change for children their families, and their communities. SCiPNGg prides itself in being a child safe organization. For more information, please visit:
www.savethechildren.org.au.
ROLE PURPOSE
The National MEAL Manager, based out of SCiPNG’s head office in Port Moresby, is responsible for the overall design and implementation of MEAL systems (including MEAL Information Systems or MIS) to ensure that all SCiPNG programs are of expected quality, have accountability mechanisms (e.g., share information, are participatory, and have feedback and reporting mechanisms relevant for PNG), and that learning is institutionalized for continuous program improvements. Working with relevant staffs, the National MEAL Manager will ensure comprehensive frameworks are in place to support program quality; enhance donor and stakeholder accountability; report on progress; and measure impact.
The National MEAL Manager will be expected to lead the design and improvement of MEAL frameworks, systems, and tools for existing and new SCiPNG program/project designs.  This includes orienting, supporting, and mentoring all relevant staffs across SCiPNG to deliver on projects’ MEAL requirements (e.g., data validation, analysis, and visualization), improving internal accountability and donor reporting.
This role reports to the Director of Program Development and Quality, requires close collaboration with the Program Operations team, and will advise the senior management team on issues relating to MEAL. The role will have direct line management of the MEAL team. The responsibilities below are not exhaustive; other tasks may be required according to changing operational and contextual needs.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT, DESIGN, AND QUALITY
Identify needs and opportunities for potential programs through situational analyses, feasibility studies, networking, and leveraging research and evaluation findings.
Catalyze MEAL engagement in all new program designs, both humanitarian and development responses, including development and responsibility for MEAL workbooks.
Ensure consistent MEAL methodology and quality benchmarks/assurance across thematic programs; ensure that all programs have effective MEAL practices throughout the program cycle.
Act as the focal point for all situation analyses, designing study methodologies, tools, and sampling strategies.
STRATEGIC DIRECTION
Provide technical support for developing, reviewing and updating the Country Strategy Plan.
Participate in the Country Annual Planning and Country Annual Reporting, providing oversight and compiling of reports (e.g., Total Reach, strategy goal indicators).
Provide thought leadership and links with Save the Children Australia’s (SCA) regional initiatives, including participation in Pacific MEAL Community of Practice.
Lead the compilation of Program Quality Key Performance Indicators, reporting on a quarterly basis.
Work with the Senior Management Team to guarantee that SCiPNG’s mandate, values, and policies are reflected throughout all operations and activities (e.g., PSEA, child safeguarding, anti-corruption, anti-fraud).
MONITORING, EVALUATION, ACCOUNTABILITY, AND LEARNING
Monitoring:
Lead in the development, implementation, and maintenance of MEAL workbook, databases, trackers, and tools, ensuring standardization of disaggregated data.
Coordinate with relevant program and partner staffs on the most viable data collection method(s) for each project targets/research agenda and on providing timely inputs (i.e., data collection that documents progress against targets) required for all SCiPNG and donor reporting (e.g., Total Reach, global outcome indicators, performance trackers, databases). Ensure that all reporting is of high quality and submitted in a timely manner.
Work with program and partner staffs to develop selection of project participants; develop and supervise systems to maintain confidential project participant records.
Support program and partner staff to use digital data collection methods (i.e. Kobo).
Accountability:
Ensure that MEAL, program, and partner staffs have a clear understanding on program accountability to children and communities through training and coaching.
Ensure that Feedback and Reporting Mechanisms (FRMs) are functional; provide follow-up and support for the investigation of serious complaints and feedback as needed per the established protocols.
Meet with partner organizations to request feedback and follow-up on critical issues and/or complaints from project participants.
Ensure that periodic MEAL reports are stored and debriefed at different levels, and that action plans for addressing quality gaps are developed and followed up.
Evaluation and
Learning:
Take lead in conducting/facilitating strategic program evaluations and after-action reviews.
Work with MEAL, program, and partner staffs to develop evaluation (e.g., baseline, mid-term, final) Terms of Reference, methodologies, tools, and sampling strategies. Oversee surveys of program/project impact to ensure that deliverables are on target. Act as the focal point for all evaluations – both internal and external.
Promote cross-thematic and cross-program learning; establish quarterly reflection, reviews, and consolidation of feedback across all programs.
MANAGEMENT INFORMATION SYSTEM
Manage automated data pipeline (SC system) for PNG and scale-up of projects with PowerBI Dashboards.
Provide data analysis to the relevant program staff to support improvements to program quality and contributions to donor reporting.
Analyze and present data to senior management to be able to make strategic programmatic decisions.
Analyze and present client feedback data to ensure the organization's program is client centered.
CAPACITY BUILDING
In coordination with Program Operations, provide ongoing and one-off technical MEAL support and advice to programs and partners.
Ensure that core MEAL training modules and approaches are effectively rolled out.
COORDINATION AND REPRESENTATION
Liaise with MEAL focal persons from Pacific Regional Office, Save the Children Australia and other Save the Children members for sharing, learning, and updates on new developments on MEAL and related requirements.
Identify relevant technical assistance providers and pull technical assistance as needed for strengthening MEAL systems in PNG.
Represent the SCiPNG through participation in national, regional, and global MEAL initiatives as needed.
General
Comply with Save the Children policies and practices with respect to child safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, equal opportunities, and other relevant policies and procedures
Undertake any other reasonable duty as may be assigned by the line manager.
PERSON SPECIFICATIONS
Mandatory Qualifications and Experience
Minimum bachelor’s degree in political science, social sciences, development studies, communications, or other relevant field of study. Master’s level education is preferred.
Minimum of eight (8) years of relevant experience with NGOs in monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning reporting – with progressively more responsible positions.
Documented experience in successfully leading and implementing MEAL activities – system design, programmatic quality audits, systematic tracking and analysis, surveys, assessment systems and evaluations.
Thorough knowledge of results-based monitoring frameworks.
Extensive experience in working with digital data collection (i.e. Kobo), data analysis (e.g., Excel) and data visualization (e.g., PowerBI) applications. High level of computer proficiency with a particular focus on MS Word, MS Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint.
Experience integrating quality standards in programs and implementing accountability initiatives, such as child participation, information sharing, and feedback and reporting mechanisms.
A good understanding of and experience in addressing gender-related challenges in monitoring and evaluation of programs.
Ability to think strategically, prioritise, and meet deadlines in a complex and challenging environment; must be culturally sensitive.
Exhibit a strong work ethic with a high degree of flexibility with respect to working hours; ability to effectively plan and manage own time under pressure.
Excellent writing and verbal skills in English for reports and communications documents. Ability to write clear reports including data analysis and triangulation.
Proven ability to supervise, train, and coach staff. Previous experience in managing consultants is desirable.
Documented experience in supporting successful funding proposals to donors.
Desirable Knowledge and Experience
Experience with international donor (e.g., DFAT, MFAT) regulations, project design, and reporting requirements.
Experience of different evaluation approaches (e.g., RCTs, quasi-experimental designs, Most Significant Change, outcome harvesting).
Experience with quantitative and qualitative data analysis software (e.g. STATA, SPSS, NVivo, Atlas.ti).
Previous experience of working within a Payment by Results framework.
Skills/Abilities
Strong analytical, relationship building, negotiation, and interpersonal skills.
High level of attention to detail and quality.
High level strategic planning skills.
Willingness to travel to regional areas of PNG.
Strong time management and organizational skills.
CHILD SAFEGUARDING
This position may require the post holder to have regular contact with children or access to children and young people either frequently or intensive

Position Description

Here you’ll make a difference
Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organisation, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea (PNG), Save the Children implements programs in the sectors of health and nutrition, education, child protection, child rights governance, and livelihoods. The PNG Country Program is looking for an Advocacy and Partnerships Manager who will provide technical leadership in advocacy and partner management for all programming in PNG.
Save the Children in Papua New Guinea (SCiPNG) is committed to be a platform for transformative and lasting change for children their families, and their communities. SCiPNG prides itself in being a child safe organization. For more information, please visit:
www.savethechildren.org.au
.
Here your skills will be valued - Role Purpose
The Advocacy and Partnerships Manager will lead the designing and delivery of Save the Children’s advocacy and communication strategy and the building and maintaining of key strategic partnerships that influence legal and policy decisions, inspire public support and engagement, and drive the agenda for children in Papua New Guinea (PNG).
The Advocacy and Partnerships Manager is expected to lead on initiatives aimed to improve children’s lives at national, provincial and community levels, including policy advocacy, strategic communications, media engagement and campaigning. She/he will be expected to build and maintain strong partnerships with key stakeholders including government representatives, civil society organisations, INGOs, NGOs, and academia. Working with the Program Development and Quality Director, she/he will lead on the development and implementation of Save the Children’s Advocacy, Communications, Campaigns and Media (ACCM) Strategy in PNG.
The Advocacy and Partnerships Manager, in coordination with the Communications Officer, will be responsible for managing the SCiPNG’s media-related activities – including its social media and online platforms – to ensure published information is up to date, of high quality, accurate, and in line with organisational policies and procedures.
She/he will also support the capacity building of SCiPNG staff in identifying and undertaking advocacy and communications to achieve brand consistency in line with organizational policy standards and donor requirements.
Dimensions:
The Advocacy and Partnerships Manager has both an internal and external orientation but works closely with the Program Development and Quality (PDQ) team, the Regional Pacific Policy and Advocacy Advisor, the Regional Pacific Communications Lead and program implementation teams to facilitate the planning, implementation, and monitoring of advocacy, media and communication initiatives. Externally, the role will be expected to strategically position SCiPNG as a leading provider of life changing interventions for children and their families.
Working contacts
Internal:
PDQ team members, program managers and various implementation team members, thematic leads, consultants, visitors, communication and advocacy teams from the regional office and Save the Children member countries.
External:
Media, child rights groups, other civil society organisations, service providers, governments, local authorities, and development partners (local and international).
Key Areas of Accountability
Advocacy
In collaboration with the PDQ Director, lead the development and implementation of SCiPNG’s advocacy strategy that advances child rights at national and regional levels, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities and global frameworks.
Conduct high‑quality policy and legal framework analysis and engage with government, donors, and key national actors to influence policy and legislative reforms.
Engage with MEAL teams to generate, synthesise, and translate evidence into compelling advocacy messages, positioning paper, and briefs.
Support thematic advisors and program teams to integrate advocacy activities through developing a calendar of events and identifying key moments to deliver on the SCiPNG advocacy objectives.
Build and maintain effective, collaborative relationships with ACCM team members in Save the Children’s Australia and other Pacific Country Offices to ensure common messages and effective advocacy efforts.
Support SCiPNG’s engagement in regional and global advocacy efforts to highlight achievements.
Campaigning
Support the development of advocacy campaigns at national, regional, and global levels with children and youth activists.
Ensure meaningful, safe, and inclusive child participation in campaigns that is aligned with safeguarding and ethical standards.
Work closely with thematic advisors involved in public mobilisation and engagement to create moments and opportunities for campaigning.
Build and maintain effective, collaborative relationships with Save the Children’s Australia, Pacific Country Offices, Pacific regional and global advocacy teams, ensuring consistent approaches, common messages and effective campaign events.
Communications and Media
External: manage the development and implementation of a Strategic Communications Plan and guidelines for the Country Office.
Internal: manage the development and implementation of an Internal Communications Plan.
Oversee the development and quality of communication material, ensuring messages are adequate for the target audience, safe, ethical and culturally grounded.
Ensure branding consistency and donor communication compliance, including of digital media and social media.
Effectively manage external media relations.
Partnerships
Build and maintain effective relationships with government stakeholders, civil society representatives, UN, INGOs, child-led and youth groups, and Academia to advance Save the Children’s advocacy and communication efforts.
Build the capabilities of local and civil society partners through mentoring and the implementation of partner development plans that strengthen governance, program quality, reporting, and accountability.
Provide oversight of partnerships to ensure alignment with Save the Children’s partnership principles, approaches, and compliance requirements.
Designing, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning
Contribute to proposal development processes where advocacy and communication activities are present and explore opportunities for children’s voices to be heard in project designs.
With support from Save the Children Australia, develop and put in place systems to monitor and measure the impact of the PNG ACCM.
Manage the development of impact stories and share with Save the Children Australia and its Pacific Team, Pacific regional and global working groups, and/or communities of practice.
General

Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policies, procedures, work instructions and training, including all reporting requirements and processes.
Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.

27902.description:
POSITION DESCRIPTION
TITLE
SENIOR WASH TECHNICAL OFFICER
REPORTING TO
ENB SENIOR PROGRAM MANAGER & DOTTED LINE TO WASH ADVISOR
LOCATION
WATERAID -EAST NEW BRITAIN, PAPUA NEW GUINEA
CLASSIFICATION
E
EMPLOYMENT DETAILS/HOURS
Permanent,
Three-year contract (subject to three months’ probation)
Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive and climate resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is on the National Capital District and Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province and East New Britain Province.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
WaterAid passionately believes everyone in the organisation has a role to play in innovation, encourages curiosity about the world and empowering everyone to act. We recognise that both big and small changes can have positive impacts on our roles, our team and our mission.
About the Project
The PacFresH2O (Protecting Freshwater Resources for Increased Climate Resilience in the Pacific Islands) project is a multi-year initiative running from February 2024 to January 2031, aimed at enhancing climate resilience in rural communities of Papua New Guinea (PNG) and the Solomon Islands (SLB). Funded through the International Climate Initiative (IKI) and led by GIZ in partnership with the Pacific Community (SPC) and various national government bodies, the project responds to pressing climate-related challenges like drought, flooding, and cyclones that threaten water resources and infrastructure. It seeks to address the low levels of access to safe drinking water—particularly in rural and marginalised communities through integrated water management and sustainable, community-based interventions.
The project’s core strategy is built around three outputs: strengthening governance, coordination, and data use; implementing phased, climate-resilient water and sanitation solutions; and embedding Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) priorities into national policy frameworks. A key focus is on showcasing underutilised resources such as groundwater, improving meteorological and hydrological capabilities, and training local and national actors, including women and marginalised groups in climate finance and evidence-based water resource management. Through these efforts, PacFresH2O aims to create scalable and replicable models for rural water resilience, boosting the adaptive capacity of Pacific Island nations in the face of climate change
Position Summary
The Senior WASH Technical Officer will support in the implementation and partner management projects delivering improved health outcomes through inclusive and equitable water, sanitation and hygiene across PNG.
The Senior WASH Technical Officer works closely with WaterAid Technical Advisor and the wider program and partners’ teams in providing technical assistance to infrastructure projects now focusing on the PACFRESH & KIWA project in Pomio & Rabaul Districts in the East New Britain Province. The individual has critical knowledge and skills to design, cost effective and quality infrastructure and to oversee quality control of implemented activities by contractors, partners, etc.
Key Performance Areas/Accountabilities
Program Management
Lead on design of appropriate, cost effective, sustainable and inclusive WASH infrastructure that responds to local contextual factors in various districts in East New Britain.
Develop accurate bills of quantities.
Ensure that programs and projects satisfy minimum criteria defined in WaterAid Guidelines and PNG Government policy, law and regulation, and are implemented in line with grant requirements, budgets and plans, including by overseeing work of construction partners.
Ensure to review the project workplan, MEL framework, risk matrix and RAG rating data are updated on WaterAid Programme System (WAPS) on a monthly, quarterly and bi-annually.
Work with the WASH Technical Advisor, East New Senior Program Manager and Program Officers to prepare and deliver project implementation plans that take into account project/grant requirements, partner engagement and capacity, and good development practice (sustainable, collaborative, empowering, rights based).
Work with Program Officers to provide guidance to the WaterAid team on hygiene and sanitation behaviour change approaches and support the team to ensure ‘good practice’ approaches are pursued at all times.
Arrange meetings with WaSH Committees/partners/constructors to agree on designs, construction approaches, negotiate contracts, build capacity of construction partners and local technician in the community, monitor progress of infrastructure construction; identify and manage any risks.
Lead contracting and procurement of goods and services of the projects are documented in consultation with the WASH Advisor for approval by the Country Director in a timely manner.
Ensure timely processing of acquittals and follow up with partners/contractors. Ensure activities are implemented in accordance with the design, scope of work and available budget.

28005.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
Join a high-performing maintenance engineering team where your expertise will directly influence the reliability, efficiency, and future performance of a world-renowned processing plant. In this role, you will be instrumental in supporting major plant improvement initiatives helping to increase throughput, optimise asset performance, and ensure safe, sustainable operations. You'll bring your technical knowledge and problem-solving capability to a team eager to learn from experienced professionals and make a lasting impact on the business.
As part of our team, you will
Execute maintenance engineering activities to support critical plant assets and infrastructure.
Develop and implement preventive maintenance strategies that improve equipment reliability and operational performance.
Work closely with operations, maintenance planning, reliability, and engineering design teams to deliver maintenance solutions.
Identify asset performance risks, investigate system failures, and recommend practical, value-driven improvements.
Provide technical advice and guidance to resolve maintenance challenges and support plant optimisation initiatives.
Contribute to a culture of safety, quality, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
Collaborate with site stakeholders and the global asset management team to share best practices and implement innovative solutions.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To be successful, you will bring:
A degree in Engineering with demonstrated experience in maintenance engineering environments.
Ideally 5+ years of experience within processing plants, heavy industry, mining, or material handling environments.
Specialist knowledge of crushing and material handling systems.
Eligibility for, or attainment of, IEPNG accreditation.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to develop practical solutions in fast-paced operational environments.
A commitment to quality, safety, and continuous improvement.
Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to build productive relationships across multiple disciplines.
Experience in quality assurance, quality control, inspection activities, or holding a trade qualification will be highly regarded.
Your work environment
You'll join a close-knit and supportive maintenance engineering team, reporting to the Maintenance Engineering Supervisor and working alongside reliability engineers, design engineers, planners, and operational stakeholders. The team is focused on lifting plant performance and investing in the future capability of the operation.
This role offers exposure to a globally recognised processing operation, opportunities to collaborate with international asset management networks, and the chance to build a long-term engineering career. Career progression pathways include opportunities to move into Supervisor and Superintendent roles, as well as broaden your experience across different plant areas and specialised engineering disciplines.

27996.description:
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources & Environment (PNGUNRE)
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources & Environment (PNGUNRE) invites applications from suitably qualified and experienced professionals for the position of Occupational Health, Safety & Environment (OHSE) Officer within the Human Resources Department.
PNGUNRE is committed to strengthening governance, operational efficiency, employee wellbeing and environmental sustainability across the University. As part of its ongoing institutional improvement agenda, the University is seeking a proactive and results-oriented Occupational Health, Safety & Environment professional to coordinate the University's workplace health, safety and environmental management framework and foster a culture of safety, compliance and continuous improvement across all campuses.
About the Role
Reporting directly to the Human Resource Manager, the Occupational Health, Safety & Environment (OHSE) Officer is responsible for coordinating and implementing PNGUNRE's occupational health, safety and environmental management programs to promote a safe, healthy, compliant and environmentally responsible workplace.
The successful candidate will coordinate workplace inspections, hazard identification, risk assessments, incident investigations, emergency preparedness, environmental management initiatives and workplace safety awareness programs while ensuring compliance with relevant legislation and University policies.
Working closely with Schools, Departments, Divisions, managers and employees, the successful applicant will provide professional advice and operational support to strengthen workplace safety systems, minimise organisational risks and promote employee wellbeing throughout the University.
The position will play an important role in strengthening institutional compliance, improving workplace safety performance and supporting PNGUNRE's commitment to environmental stewardship and operational excellence.
Key Responsibilities
The successful candidate will be responsible for:
Occupational Health and Safety Management
Coordinating the implementation of PNGUNRE's Occupational Health, Safety and Environment Management Framework.
Assisting in the development, review and implementation of OHSE policies, procedures, guidelines and safe work practices.
Promoting compliance with occupational health and safety legislation, regulations and University policies.
Maintaining the University's OHSE documentation, registers and records.
Providing professional advice to management, staff, contractors and visitors on workplace health and safety matters.
Promoting a proactive safety culture across all University campuses.
Workplace Inspections and Risk Management
Conducting regular workplace inspections across university campuses, facilities and operational areas.
Identifying workplace hazards and unsafe work practices and recommending appropriate corrective actions.
Undertaking workplace risk assessments and maintaining hazard and risk registers.
Monitoring implementation of approved risk control measures.
Assisting departments in developing safe work procedures and workplace risk mitigation strategies.
Incident Reporting and Investigation
Coordinating reporting and recording of workplace incidents, accidents, injuries and near misses.
Conducting workplace incident investigations and preparing investigation reports.
Identifying root causes and recommending corrective and preventive actions.
Monitoring implementation of investigation recommendations.
Maintaining incident statistics and analysing workplace safety trends.
Workplace Safety Training and Awareness
Developing and delivering workplace health and safety awareness programs.
Coordinating OHSE induction programs for new employees and contractors.
Promoting emergency procedures and safe work practices.
Supporting specialised safety training, including fire safety, first aid and emergency response.
Developing workplace safety awareness materials and campaigns.
Emergency Preparedness and Environmental Management
Assisting in developing and maintaining University emergency response plans.
Coordinating emergency drills, evacuation exercises and emergency response activities.
Supporting environmental management initiatives, waste management and sustainability programs.
Monitoring environmental compliance and promoting environmentally responsible workplace practices.
Liaising with relevant emergency services and regulatory authorities where required.
Compliance Monitoring and OHSE Reporting
Conducting internal OHSE compliance inspections and safety audits.
Assisting with external inspections and regulatory reviews.
Maintaining OHSE registers, compliance documentation and statutory records.
Preparing monthly, quarterly and annual OHSE reports.
Providing recommendations to management for continuous improvement of workplace health, safety and environmental performance.
HR Advisory Support
Providing professional OHSE advice and support to Human Resources and University management.
Supporting employee wellness initiatives and Health & Safety Committee activities.
Assisting with the development and review of OHSE policies and procedures.
Supporting organisational improvement initiatives and performing other duties as directed by the Human Resource Manager.
Qualifications & Experience
Essential Requirements
Applicants must possess:
A Bachelor's Degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Health, Environmental Science, Public Health, Safety Management, Human Resource Management or a related discipline.
A minimum of three (3) years' relevant experience in occupational health and safety, workplace compliance, environmental management or a related field.
Sound knowledge of occupational health and safety principles, legislation and workplace risk management practices.
Demonstrated experience conducting workplace inspections, hazard identification, risk assessments and incident investigations.
Experience preparing safety reports, compliance documentation and workplace records.
Strong organisational, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
Desirable Qualifications
Preference will be given to applicants with:
Experience working within a university, statutory authority or public sector organisation.
Knowledge of Papua New Guinea occupational health, safety and environmental legislation and regulatory requirements.
Experience developing OHSE policies, procedures and safety management systems.
Experience conducting workplace safety audits and environmental compliance reviews.
Knowledge of environmental sustainability and workplace wellness initiatives.
Membership of a recognised Occupational Health and Safety professional body.
Key Competencies
The ideal candidate should demonstrate:
Sound knowledge of occupational health, safety and environmental management principles.
Ability to coordinate workplace inspections, hazard identification and risk assessments.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to investigate workplace incidents and identify root causes.
Ability to develop and deliver workplace safety awareness and training programs.
Strong organisational and administrative capability.
Excellent interpersonal and stakeholder engagement skills.
High attention to detail and accuracy.
Ability to interpret legislation, policies and workplace safety procedures.
Strong report writing and documentation skills.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.
Integrity, professionalism and the ability to maintain strict confidentiality.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Terms & Conditions
Appointment will be made in accordance with the PNGUNRE Terms and Conditions of Employment.
Performance will be assessed through the University's Performance Management System.
The successful applicant may be required to travel between university campuses and external agencies as required.
The position requires regular workplace inspections and may involve work in laboratories, workshops, farms, construction sites and other operational environments.
University accommodation is not a condition of employment. Preference will be given to applicants who are residents of East New Britain Province or those who are willing to relocate and are able to secure and meet their own accommodation arrangements.
Salary Range
Base Salary: K25, 843.00 – K31, 586.00
Why Join PNGUNRE?
PNGUNRE offers an excellent opportunity to contribute to strengthening workplace health, safety and environmental management within Papua New Guinea's specialist university for natural resources and environment.
The successful candidate will play an important role in improving workplace safety systems, strengthening legislative compliance, enhancing employee wellbeing, supporting environmental sustainability and advancing the University's commitment to operational excellence and institutional development.
Application Details
Interested applicants should submit:
A written application addressing the selection criteria.
A current Curriculum Vitae (CV).
Certified copies of qualifications and other relevant certificates.
Contact details of at least three (3) current professional referees.
Applications should be addressed to:
The Human Resources Manager
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources & Environment
Private Mail Bag
Kokopo, East New Britain Province
Papua New Guinea
Or email applications to:
[email protected]
Closing Date: Friday, 14 August 2026
PNGUNRE is an equal opportunity employer.
Apply

27994.description:
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources & Environment (PNGUNRE)
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources & Environment (PNGUNRE) invites applications from suitably qualified and experienced professionals for the position of HR Officer – Performance Management within the Human Resources Department.
PNGUNRE is committed to strengthening governance, operational efficiency, employee accountability and service delivery across the University. As part of its ongoing institutional improvement agenda, the University is seeking a proactive and results-oriented Human Resource professional to coordinate the University's performance management framework and support the development of a high-performance culture across the institution.
About the Role
Reporting directly to the Human Resource Manager, the HR Officer – Performance Management is responsible for coordinating and administering PNGUNRE’s employee performance management processes to promote accountability, productivity, continuous improvement and effective workforce performance.
The successful candidate will manage key performance management activities including performance planning, KPI development, performance reviews, probation monitoring, performance improvement processes and performance reporting.
Working closely with Schools, Departments, Divisions, managers and employees, the successful applicant will provide professional HR support to ensure performance expectations are clearly defined, monitored and aligned with PNGUNRE’s strategic objectives.
The position will play an important role in strengthening employee performance, improving organisational effectiveness and supporting a culture of accountability and continuous improvement across the University.
Key Responsibilities
The successful candidate will be responsible for:
Performance Management Administration
Coordinating the implementation and administration of PNGUNRE’s employee performance management system across the University.
Developing and maintaining annual performance management schedules, including performance planning, mid-year reviews and annual assessments.
Providing guidance and support to managers and employees on performance management requirements, processes and documentation.
Monitoring completion of employee performance agreements and performance reviews.
Maintaining accurate and confidential performance management records.
Preparing regular updates and reports on performance management activities for the Human Resource Manager.
Ensuring performance management processes are conducted fairly, consistently and in accordance with approved University policies and procedures.
Performance Planning and KPI Management
Assisting managers and supervisors in developing appropriate performance objectives, Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and work expectations.
Supporting alignment of individual employee performance goals with university strategic priorities, operational plans and departmental objectives.
Providing advice on establishing measurable and achievable performance targets.
Monitoring implementation of approved performance agreements and identifying areas requiring support or intervention.
Maintaining performance documentation and records for reporting and compliance purposes.
Performance Reviews and Assessment
Coordinating annual employee performance appraisal processes across Schools, Departments and Divisions.
Providing support to supervisors and employees on performance assessment requirements and rating standards.
Reviewing completed performance assessments to ensure accuracy, consistency and compliance with university requirements.
Analysing performance trends and identifying recurring issues affecting employee productivity and effectiveness.
Preparing performance reports and information to support management decision-making.
Ensuring performance assessment records are properly maintained and available for audit and reference purposes.
Performance Improvement and Employee Development
Supporting managers in addressing employee underperformance through appropriate performance improvement processes.
Assisting in the development and monitoring of Performance Improvement Plans (PIPs).
Providing advice on strategies to improve employee performance, accountability and workplace effectiveness.
Identifying learning and development needs arising from performance reviews.
Supporting HR initiatives aimed at improving employee capability, productivity and organisational performance.
Promoting a culture of professionalism, continuous improvement and performance excellence.
Probation Management and Performance Monitoring
Coordinating probation review processes for newly appointed employees.
Monitoring probation periods and ensuring supervisors complete required assessments within approved timelines.
Maintaining probation records and providing reports on probation status.
Supporting recommendations relating to confirmation, extension or other employment decisions based on performance outcomes.
Performance Reporting and HR Advisory Support
Preparing performance management reports including appraisal completion rates, performance trends and compliance statistics.
Maintaining accurate performance information within the Human Resource Information System and relevant databases.
Providing professional advice and customer-focused support to managers and employees on performance management matters.
Assisting with HR projects, workforce productivity initiatives, organisational improvement activities and other duties as directed by the Human Resource Manager.
Qualifications & Experience
Essential Requirements
Applicants must possess:
A Bachelor's Degree in Human Resource Management, Business Administration, Management, Public Administration or a related discipline.
A minimum of three (3) years' relevant experience in Human Resource Management, with demonstrated experience in performance management, employee development or HR advisory services.
Sound knowledge of performance management principles, systems and practices.
Experience coordinating employee performance reviews, appraisals and performance documentation.
Understanding of employee productivity, workforce improvement strategies and HR reporting requirements.
Strong organisational, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and Human Resource Information Systems.
Desirable Qualifications
Preference will be given to applicants with:
Experience working within a university, statutory authority or public sector organisation.
Knowledge of PNG employment practices, Public Service requirements and HR policies.
Experience developing Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and performance improvement plans.
Experience using HR Information Systems for performance tracking and reporting.
Membership of a recognised Human Resource professional body.
Key Competencies
The ideal candidate should demonstrate:
Sound knowledge of performance management principles and practices.
Ability to coordinate performance planning, monitoring and review processes.
Strong analytical skills and ability to interpret HR data.
Ability to support managers in managing employee performance issues.
Strong organisational and administrative capability.
Excellent interpersonal and customer service skills.
High attention to detail and accuracy.
Ability to interpret policies and procedures.
Strong report writing and documentation skills.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.
Integrity, professionalism and ability to maintain strict confidentiality.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team.
Terms & Conditions
Appointment will be made in accordance with the PNGUNRE Terms and Conditions of Employment.
Performance will be assessed through the University's Performance Management System.
The successful applicant may be required to travel to university campuses and external agencies as required.
University accommodation is not a condition of employment. Preference will be given to applicants who are residents of East New Britain Province or those who are willing to relocate and are able to secure and meet their own accommodation arrangements.

Specialist – HR Information Systems
About the role
Reporting to the Senior, Specialist HRIS, the Specialist - HRIS is responsible for implementing and maintaining HR Information management systems for the business. The role provides Information System support to maintain data integrity, accuracy, consistency and security of all HR information in HR Oracle, related-databases and records, as well as providing technical support and training to HR Staff and end-users.

Administer, support and maintain HR Information systems and other NPL application tools (e.g. ID Facial Recognition system)
Manage HR Oracle and Element
Ensure effective interface with Oracle payroll systems and In Flight
Based on ad hoc requirements, be able to query data from the SQL server for analysis and reporting, or to set up customised reports and dashboards using the MS Business Intelligence Development Studio
Lead regular systems audits to ensure data integrity, accuracy and consistency is maintained across HR Oracle system and other related systems
Conduct regular system audits to ensure data integrity, accuracy and consistency is maintained across HR Oracle system and other filing databases/records system

You will demonstrate a ‘One Team’ approach, providing effective leadership and development for your local team to reinforce NPL’s culture and values, always promoting a safe work environment.  The position requires a high energy individual, hands-on management style and desire to continuously improve you and your team’s knowledge and systems and methods of work.

A university qualification (Diploma/Degree) in HR Management, Information Technology, or any business or science/applied science discipline with a strong data analytics and reporting focus
Experience (3-5 years) in HR or Systems and Application professions, with a working knowledge of HR metrics, standards, policies and processes

Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a

27954.description:
Estimator
The accurate, no-surprises kind
Location:
Atlas, Port Moresby
Employment:
Full-time, Local Hire
Important:
If you do not have proven estimating, quantity take-off, tendering, or construction costing experience, please do not submit your CV.
Atlas is part of the Kenmore Group of Companies and supports projects across steel fabrication, modular housing, building, and civil works.
We’re looking for an experienced Estimator to join our Port Moresby team and prepare accurate, competitive, and timely cost estimates, budgets, and tender submissions.
This is not a role for someone who guesses numbers or waits until the last minute. We need someone who can read drawings properly, understand scopes of work, price jobs accurately, manage tender deadlines, and support the business with reliable cost information.
If your experience is limited, this is not the one to test it on.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be responsible for preparing detailed quantity take-offs, Bills of Quantities, cost estimates, tender submissions, quotations, budgets, and pricing schedules.
That includes reviewing drawings, specifications, scopes of work, supplier quotes, subcontractor pricing, labour, materials, plant, preliminaries, and commercial risks before a submission goes out.
You’ll also support the commercial and project teams with handover budgets, variation pricing, cost advice, tender records, supplier pricing updates, and post-tender reviews.
You’ll work closely with managers, project teams, design and drafting staff, sales, clients, consultants, subcontractors, and suppliers to make sure pricing is accurate and commercially sound.
The expectation is simple: price the job properly, protect the margin, and help Atlas win the right work.
Who This Suits
This role suits an experienced Estimator, Quantity Surveyor, or construction professional with strong estimating experience.
You understand construction drawings, specifications, contract documents, BOQs, tender requirements, supplier pricing, subcontractor pricing, and project cost control.
You should be confident working with Excel and, ideally, estimating or take-off software.
You know how to work under tender pressure without letting accuracy drop. You can manage multiple tenders, keep records organised, and flag risks before they become problems.
You are detailed, commercially aware, organised, and able to communicate clearly with both internal teams and external suppliers.
If people already rely on you to get the numbers right, this will feel familiar.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
Atlas is involved in real construction, steel, building, modular housing, and civil works projects.
You’ll be part of a business where accurate estimating directly supports project delivery, commercial decisions, and company growth.
This is a role where detail matters, good pricing is valued, and strong commercial discipline is taken seriously.
How to Apply
If you’re reading this and thinking, “I can price this properly,” then we want to hear from you.
Send your CV and cover letter to:
HR Team
[email protected]
Applications close: Saturday, 14 August 2026
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
Apply

Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE)
About the University
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNGUNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training and community development initiatives

27940.description:
Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE)
About the University
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNGUNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training and community development initiatives
The University emphasises practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, and strong industry collaboration, producing graduates who are work-ready and capable of contributing meaningfully to sustainable development outcomes across Papua New Guinea.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from suitably qualified and motivated candidates for appointment as Tutor (Technical Instructor) – Agriculture Marketing and Supply Chain within the Department of Agriculture, School of Natural Resources.
This position supports undergraduate teaching through tutorials, practical classes, applied learning activities, and academic support in agriculture marketing, agribusiness, and supply chain systems. The role contributes to undergraduate instruction, applied research support, extension and industry engagement activities, and academic administration aligned with PNGUNRE’s mandate in sustainable agriculture and market-oriented development.
The successful appointee will work under the direction of an assigned Lecturer and Strand Leader and report to the Head of Department, Agriculture.
Key Responsibilities
Assist Lecturers in the preparation and delivery of tutorials and practical sessions in Agriculture Marketing and Supply Chain.
Support undergraduate teaching, learning activities, and applied field-based instruction.
Provide academic support, mentoring, and supervision assistance to undergraduate students, including guidance on assignments and projects.
Assist with assessment preparation, marking, moderation, and submission of student results in accordance with university procedures.
Participate in applied research activities and assist with data collection, analysis, and reporting.
Support preparation of research proposals and departmental research initiatives, as required.
Contribute to extension, outreach, and industry engagement activities related to agricultural marketing and value chains.
Assist in the development and review of teaching and learning materials, including blended and digital delivery resources.
Participate in Sectional, Departmental, and University committees and activities, as required.
Assist with the preparation of quarterly and annual academic and research reports.
Ensure compliance with university academic, research, quality assurance, and administrative policies and procedures.
Undertake other duties as reasonably directed by the Lecturer, Strand Leader, or Head of Department.
Qualifications, Experience & Competency Profile
Bachelor’s degree in agriculture, Agribusiness, Agriculture Marketing, Supply Chain Management, or a closely related discipline from a recognised institution.
A master’s degree in a relevant field is desirable but not mandatory.
A minimum of one (1)–two (2) years teaching, tutoring, field extension, or relevant industry or professional experience.
Demonstrated capacity to support quality undergraduate course delivery and applied teaching in agriculture marketing and supply chain systems.
Demonstrated ability or potential to assist in supervising undergraduate students.
Basic research exposure or demonstrated interest in applied and industry-focused research.
Experience or willingness to support blended and flexible learning approaches using digital technologies.
Strong interpersonal, communication, and organisational skills.
Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams and culturally diverse environments.
Commitment to equity, cultural diversity, and workplace health and safety principles.
High standards of professionalism, ethical conduct, and integrity.

27665.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
Implementation of the complete mine power supply and distribution system; and a maintenance system for all electrical equipment in the underground mine and our exploration sites in Kainantu.  Training of T/A Electrician to effectively monitor and maintain the electrical systems in the mine, with particular reference to the electrical components.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Diagnose electrical defects or hazards on systems, appliances and machinery and identify adjustment and repair timely.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment, appliances, and machines.
Inspect, test and qualified to apply and remove ‘out-of-service’ or ‘not-to-be operated’ tags to electrical equipment, appliances, and machines.
Prepare sketches and plan layout to determine the location of electrical wiring and equipment and to always ensure safety compliance.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and machines.
Delegate routine tasks to subordinates and provide supervision where required.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair and service within the mine site area, underground and on field, or where job is required.
Work long and odd hours, and often be on call in emergency situations and extreme conditions.
Attend to physically demanding tasks involving digging ditches and moving and lifting heavy objects.
Perform general housekeeping within and around work area.
Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
Ensure that the sections daily work plans are executed as directed.
Competent in lifting and safe operation of workshop equipment.
Reading and understanding technical drawings and manuals.
Diagnose problems in all equipment with regular reference to equipment manuals.
Prepare and plan of welding jobs for site services.
Carry out equipment alignments with Dial Indicators.
Conduct accurate dimensional checks of crusher bushes, shafts or bearing clearances and recording data.
Attend to isolations required for simple tasks to major shutdowns.
Conduct general housekeeping at work area.
Identify and report safety hazards.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you should have;
Grades 10 or 12 certificate
Must be a NATTB Level 3 Electrical Mechanic Tradesman with PNG Power EW10 certification.
You should have a current NEA Electrician’s License to meet government regulations.
Must have wide experience in the installation and maintenance of underground power distribution systems, transformer installations, motor control centres, LVHV transfers, and starters; and in the maintenance of underground equipment – electric motors, compressor stations and other electrical equipment.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply
