27967.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As the
Manager, Asset Management, Fixed Plant
, you will play a critical leadership role in one of the world's premier gold mining operations, driving the performance, reliability, safety, and sustainability of Lihir’s fixed plant assets. Reporting directly to the General Manager, you will lead the asset management function, ensuring critical operational assets deliver maximum availability, productivity, and value while supporting Newmont's commitment to safety, operational excellence, and responsible mining.
This is an exceptional opportunity for a strategic and influential leader to shape the future of asset management at a world-class operation, leading large multidisciplinary teams and contributing directly to site-wide performance and business success.
As part of our leadership team, you will:
Provide visible and inspiring safety leadership, fostering a culture where safety, risk management, and critical control effectiveness are embedded in every activity.
Lead the Fixed Plant Asset Management function, ensuring assets are maintained, operated, and utilised efficiently to maximise availability and performance.
Develop and execute strategic asset management plans that align with site operational objectives and long-term business priorities.
Drive asset integrity and lifecycle management initiatives across all fixed plant assets and equipment.
Lead preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance programs to optimise equipment reliability and operational performance.
Monitor, analyse, and report on asset performance trends, identifying opportunities for continuous improvement and operational excellence.
Lead and develop a high-performing team of superintendents, supervisors, technicians, operators, and contractors.
Manage maintenance partnerships, contractor relationships, and external service providers to ensure safe and effective service delivery.
Influence capital planning, cost optimisation, and business improvement initiatives that enhance asset performance and reduce operational risk.
Contribute as a key member of the Lihir leadership team, supporting site-wide performance, culture, safety, and operational delivery.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To thrive in this position, you will bring deep technical expertise, strong leadership capability, and a passion for building safe, high-performing teams.
Extensive experience in Asset Management, Fixed Plant Operations, Processing, Maintenance, or a related operational leadership environment.
Experience in large-scale mineral processing or major mining operations will be highly regarded.
Experience leading asset management transformation, operational excellence, or reliability improvement programs.
Proven experience leading and developing large, multidisciplinary teams in a people-focused environment, with a strong track record of building capability and developing future leaders.
Inclusive leader with a proven ability to develop, mentor and empower employees, fostering high-performing teams and bringing out the best in others.
Strong experience in asset lifecycle management, maintenance strategy, reliability engineering, and continuous improvement programs.
Proven ability to optimise asset performance, availability, utilisation, and operating costs.
Experience developing and implementing preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance frameworks.
Bachelor’s Degree in engineering or a related discipline desirable.
Strong commercial acumen, including budget management, capital planning, and cost optimisation.
Demonstrated capability influencing and engaging a broad range of stakeholders, including operational leaders, contractors, regulators, and business partners.
Strong understanding of health, safety, environmental, and sustainability requirements within a mining or heavy industrial environment.
Your work environment
Located at Newmont's world-class Lihir Operation, you will join a diverse and collaborative leadership team committed to delivering safe, reliable, and sustainable performance.
Working closely with operational, technical, commercial, safety, and business improvement teams, you will have the opportunity to influence critical operational outcomes while developing future capability across the organisation.
This is a highly visible leadership role where your expertise will directly impact operational performance, asset reliability, production outcomes, and workforce development.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a residential 5:2 roster, based in Newmont’s Lihir townsite community, a gated precinct based on the coastline cliff with magnificent ocean views.
The townsite has Company provided housing (inc. utilities), international school (up to and including Year 10) and a range of recreational facilities including gym, sports club with restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts and playground areas for the kids. There is also a 9-hole golf course on the island! Healthcare services are provided at the Lihir Medical Clinic.
An onsite deli and café provide access to fresh local and imported produce including grocery items, as well as barista-made coffees and freshly baked cakes. The company offers regular shipment of groceries and care packages for townsite residents to access goods not available on the island.
The Lihir fishing and boating clubs offer the opportunity to get out and enjoy the pristine waters and beaches around the island on the weekends.
A generous relocation package is provided to ensure smooth integration for you (and your family) to settle into island life.  You will also be eligible for medical insurance cover, annual flights home and schooling for eligible dependants. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package and bonus scheme.
Why Join Newmont
When you join Newmont, you become part of a global organisation recognised for operational excellence, innovation, safety leadership, and sustainable mining practices.
A critical leadership role with significant impact on site performance and business outcomes.
The opportunity to lead strategic asset management initiatives at a world-class mining operation.

With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.
World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of
Provincial Project Coordinator
to be based in
Kiunga, Western Province.
MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Lead and manage community coordination, ensuring effective engagement with local authorities (National Department of Health (NDoH) and Western Provincial Health Authority (WPHA)), community leaders, and stakeholders to promote awareness and participation in project activities.
Support the district project officers in planning, overseeing implementation, and monitoring project activities in alignment with project objectives and scope.
Act as the provincial focal point for all CNSP 1 project-related matters, ensuring effective communication and coordination among stakeholders, including government (NDoH, PHAs) INGOs, DDAs, LLGs and local communities.
Conduct regular field visits to monitor progress, identify challenges, and ensure corrective actions are taken to maintain project quality and effectiveness.

Identify potential risks and develop mitigation strategies to ensure the successful implementation of project activities.
Ensure all employees and affiliates are well-informed and compliant with safeguarding responsibilities to promote the safety and well-being of children, adults, clients, and beneficiaries.
Establish a strong collaborative relationship with key stakeholders, representing WVPNG in nutrition forums, and ensuring effective internal communication and alignment with  project development objectives (PDOs).
The Provincial Project Coordinator will work in close supervision of the Area Program Manager, Senior Project Coordinator, Project Manager, Finance, Monitoring and Evaluation officer and with the Area Program Team of their respective Provincial assignments.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Minimum of bachelor’s degree or college qualification social work, business economics, agriculture, health or public health, Health Management.
Good interpersonal skills and cross-cultural sensitivity
Basic understanding of project management cycle principles
Effective in written and oral communication; able to speak and write with a high standard of English.
Good networking and partnership development skills
Sound knowledge in PNG Government systems and programs
Computer literate
Communication, advocacy & facilitation skills
A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunity will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.

The Systems Administrator - Microsoft 365 will be responsible for the administration, support, and management of the company's Microsoft 365 environment. This role will ensure the smooth operation, security, and efficiency of all Microsoft 365 systems, including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, and OneDrive. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in Power Automate and Power BI to support automation and reporting needs across the organization.

1-2 years of work experience.
Experience in administering Microsoft 365 environments.
Proficiency in Power Automate for creating and managing automated workflows.
Strong experience with Power BI for developing reports and dashboards.
In-depth knowledge of Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, and OneDrive.
Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
Preferred:
Microsoft 365 Certified: Modern Desktop Administrator Associate or similar certification.
Experience with scripting languages such as PowerShell.
Knowledge of ITIL practices.
Previous experience in project management.
Key Competencies
Technical Proficiency:
Deep understanding of Microsoft 365 services and tools.
Automation Skills:
Ability to design and implement efficient automated workflows.
Analytical Thinking:
Strong data analysis skills to create meaningful Power BI reports.
Problem-Solving:
Ability to diagnose and resolve technical issues effectively.
Communication:
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Time Management:
Ability to manage multiple tasks and projects simultaneously.

Ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams.

Looking for a Change?
Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.
EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT
Supply Chain & Procurement Officer
CARE International in PNG is looking into recruiting a suitable candidate for a Supply Chain & Procurement Officer role based in Goroka, EHP. CARE is an international development and humanitarian aid organisation fighting global poverty, with a special focus on working with women and girls to bring lasting change to their communities. As a non-religious and non-political organisation, CARE works with communities to help overcome poverty by supporting development efforts and providing emergency assistance. We believe supporting women and girls is one of the most effective ways to create sustainable outcomes in poor communities.
CARE International in Papua New Guinea has a focus on Gender Equality, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Climate Change Adaptation (CCA), Agriculture and Health.
The Supply Chain & Procurement Officer is responsible to ensure that the CARE Procurement functions are efficient and adhered to. This position will also provide procurement support to other field offices.  To maintain updated inventory and asset listings in compliance with CARE’s policy and guidelines and is responsible for receiving goods; storage and stock movement (i.e. delivery of goods) and other functions are carried out in compliance with COLAM & COFM procedures.
The Supply Chain & Procurement Officer ensures program objectives are met by providing safe, compliant, efficient and effective procurement support.  In addition, Supply Chain & Procurement officer will build and maintain professional relationships with suppliers and service providers that CARE engages with.
The Supply Chain & Procurement officer is expected to facilitate efficiency and effectiveness in a team and resources towards achieving project objectives in a timely, compliant manner.
This role is based in Goroka, but will require travel to CARE PNG’s field offices and project sites as and when required.This Position has no contact with Children or vulnerable adults.
EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS:
Minimum Bachelor's degree and/ Diploma in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Logistics, or a related field and/or minimum 3 years relevant work experience in logistics and administration activities, preferably with an International Non-Government Organisation (INGO) and/or private company;
Proven experience in logistics including supply chain management and inventory control;
Demonstrated experience in following standard policies, procedures and processes and ensure the implementation of basic standard transactions;
A willingness to learn about CARE, gender equality and women’s empowerment activities;
Proven ability to manage and acquit a cash advance;
Demonstrated good interpersonal skills, sound judgment, planning, problem solving and team building skills;
Demonstrated organisational and time management skills and ability to work under pressure and to organise and manage workload to meet deadlines;
Demonstrated characteristics in honesty, reliability, trustworthiness with the ability to maintain confidentiality;
Demonstrated ability to contributes to group objectives and work effectively in a group setting;
Fluent communication skills in Pidgin and intermediate oral and written English; and
Intermediate knowledge in Microsoft Word and numeric skills with advanced Excel.

Senior Adminstration and Logistic Officer

27633.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
Implementation and maintenance and transmitting of all Radio communications equipment both underground and surface mine area
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Diagnose electrical defects or hazards on systems, appliances and machinery and identify adjustment and repair timely.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment, appliances, and machines.
Inspect, test and qualified to apply and remove ‘out-of-service’ or ‘not-to-be operated’ tags to electrical equipment, appliances, and machines.
An excellent attitude to work demonstrating Safety, Health and Environmental (SHE) and Cost Effectiveness awareness, at all times.
Assume the responsibility for all Radio Communications Equipment used by your Department by ensuring daily Pre-Start Checks are performed and defects reported immediately.
To be part of team of people that is organized attend to breakdowns and carry out daily production requirements.
Daily underground routine checks on refuge chambers, communications, Equipment radios and site wide communications.
Full comprehension that this position is highly sensitive and crucial to the company’s operations.
Keep confidential all K92 intellectual property.
To assist for ordering of parts when requested.
Offer any and all support to your Supervisor.
Any other Responsibilities as put forth by your Supervisor and/or UG Electrical Forman that are deemed reasonable and fair for the understanding of responsibilities for this position.
Complete weekly underground and 800L workshop area inspections
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you should have;
Grades 10 or 12 certificate
Tele Communications and/or Communications training certificate
Minimum of 3 - 5 years’ work experience on Communications work.
Minimum of 2 years’ experience in a similar role.
Better understanding of Communications system. Maintain current electrician’s license to meet government regulations.
The person shall have wide experience in the installation and maintenance of underground power distribution systems, transformer installations, motor control centres, LVHV transfers, and starters; and in the maintenance of underground equipment – electric motors, compressor stations and other electrical equipment.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

28084.description:
Service/Admin Driver
(The reliable, careful, no-excuses kind)
Location: PNG Motors Port Moresby
Important: If you do not have a valid driver’s licence, a clean driving record, and the discipline to handle company vehicles properly, please do not submit your CV.
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s leading automotive groups, representing brands like Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Our service and administration teams rely on dependable people who can move vehicles, support customers, assist departments, and keep daily operations running smoothly.
We’re looking for a reliable Service/Admin Driver to join our Port Moresby team and support vehicle movements, customer pick-ups and drop-offs, parts or document runs, and general service/admin duties.
This is not a role for someone who treats driving casually. You will be trusted with customer vehicles, company vehicles, documents, parts, and daily responsibilities that need to be handled properly.
If you are not punctual, careful, and responsible, this is not the one to test it on.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be responsible for safely driving customer and company vehicles as required by the service and administration teams.
That includes picking up and dropping off vehicles, assisting with customer transport, moving vehicles between departments, supporting service appointments, collecting or delivering parts, documents, and other business items, and helping with general admin/service support when required.
You’ll also help keep vehicles clean, parked correctly, and handled with care. Every vehicle must be driven responsibly, checked properly, and treated as if it belongs to the customer — because often, it does.
You may also be required to assist with basic errands, workshop support, branch coordination, and other duties that help the service team operate efficiently.
The expectation is simple: drive safely, be on time, follow instructions, and look after every vehicle properly.
Who This Suits
This role suits someone who is reliable, careful, and understands that being a driver is about more than holding a licence.
You must have a valid driver’s licence, good knowledge of Port Moresby roads, and the confidence to drive different types of vehicles safely.
You should be punctual, respectful, well-presented, and able to communicate clearly with customers, service advisors, admin staff, and workshop teams.
You need to follow instructions properly, keep records where required, report issues quickly, and avoid shortcuts that create problems for others.
If you are the kind of person who turns up on time, drives carefully, keeps calm in traffic, and can be trusted to get the job done without drama, this role will suit you.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
PNG Motors is a busy automotive business with strong brands, active workshops, and daily vehicle movement across departments.
You’ll be part of a team that depends on reliability, communication, and trust. Good drivers are important to the business because they help protect vehicles, support customers, and keep service operations moving.
This is a role where responsibility matters, good attitude is noticed, and dependable people are valued.
How to Apply
If you’re reading this and thinking, “I can be trusted with this,” then we want to hear from you.
Send your CV and cover letter to:
Dylan Siketa
[email protected]
Applications close Monday, 24 August 2026
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
Apply

27635.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
Working as part of the exploration team, the primary purpose of this position is to monitor and reduce costs associated with the Exploration Surface Operations, and ensuring Helicopters contracted operate within contractual requirements.
.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Oversee that the helicopters flight schedules and daily operations with contractors and continuously evaluate and improve helicopter operations to increase efficiency and reduce costs within optimal load.
Ensure open communication with all relevant stakeholders. Facilitate and chair meetings including Exploration, Helicopter Contractor, QED, CA and Landowner groups.
Develop and maintain a cost control system for the exploration projects, including cost tracking, forecasting, and reporting. Analyze project costs and variances to identify areas of potential savings.
About You
To be considered for this role, you must be an experienced Travel Agent with experience in either the Mining, Construction, Engineering or Oil and Gas industries. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.
Excellent customer service and communication skills.
Well-developed planning and organizational skills.
Computer proficiency in MS Office suite especially excels.
Ability to solve problems and find solutions swiftly.
Ability to work with minimum supervision.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

27986.description:
Assistant Budget Coordinator- Budget Coordination Unit, Grade 12
JOB DESCRIPTION
To assist in providing analysis and advice relating to the timing and framework for Budget preparation and overall coordination of the Budget process, including guidance to agencies and liaison with other central agencies.
JOB RESPONSIBILITIES
Assists the more senior officers in the Budget Coordination Unit to develop, promote and coordinate the implementation of an effective budget framework and timetable. The Assistant Budget Coordinator supports budget coordination through contributions to oral and written briefs, analysis and preparation of reports to Treasury Management and Ministers.
MAJOR DUTIES
Assist in the preparation of advice for management, central agencies and the Minister on the framework, timetable and overall coordination of the preparation and execution of the annual budget.
Assist in the planning of specific elements of the Budget process including: drafting and developing budget circulars, budget policies and budget rules for promulgation to Budget Operations Division staff and agencies; the formulation of timetables, the management of clearance processes and the documentation of each process, including the storage and retention of both electronic and hardcopy files.
Ensure that planned activities are performed in accordance with the approved divisional work program.
Assist in Athe coordination of quarterly budget reviews and the preparation of the National Budget Timetable and Budget Circulars.
Assess budget proposals for increased funding received outside the annual budget and provide high quality briefing and draft correspondence to the Minister/Secretary/Deputy Secretary/First Assistant Secretary as required.
Prepare briefs and draft responses to correspondences on budgetary matters.
JOB REQUIREMENTS
QUALIFICATIONS & ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
Essential
Qualifications:
A Bachelor Degree in Accounting, Commerce or Economics from a recognised university or tertiary institution.
Work experience:
Prior work experience in a previous Accounting, Commerce or Economics role or a related field.
Teamwork:
Able to work well with colleagues, respond to requests in a timely manner and share relevant information with the Division, the Department and with other stakeholders. Contribute to identifying any team development needs and building the capacity and capability of the team.
Workload and time management:
Contribute to identifying team priorities, and share or allocate specific tasks within team and to ensure competing deadlines are met. Manage own tasks within this environment. Promote effective and efficient service delivery.
Strategic and budget planning skills:
Contribute, as required, to identifying divisional and department strategic goals and budget plans and assist in the preparation of related documentation to support the meeting of these strategic goals and budget plans, as necessary.
Financial management:
Ensure all expenditure, acquittals and other financial and commercial transactions strictly adhere to Departmental and Government-wide policies and/or legislation.
Legislative knowledge:
Establish knowledge about the range of Acts, laws and policies governing the work of this role and the Department of Treasury more broadly.
Values:
Demonstrate and practice high levels of integrity, honesty, accountability, respect and wisdom and accept responsibility for one's own actions at all times.
Zero tolerance of any unethical activity or behavior:
Must be a positive role model on ethical behavior for staff and demonstrate personal qualities of honesty, fairness and professionalism.
Computing:
Demonstrate proficiency in the use of email and internet, in the application of software such as MS Word and MS Excel to perform tasks, and in the creation of presentations using MS PowerPoint.
Desirable
Work experience:
Previous experience at an equivalent level of employment with similar levels of responsibility.
Technical:
A demonstrated knowledge/understanding of Microsoft Word, Excel and related applications and a knowledge/understanding of the following legislation, policies and systems: o Public Finance (Management) Act and related instructions o Organic Law on Provincial & Local Level Governments o Public Service (Management) Act and General Orders o Public Service Policies on Accounting, Procedures and Systems o Government Accounting Systems o Appropriation Acts.

Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.
World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of
Education Officer - X3
to be based in
Lae, Morobe Province, Hagen , Western Highlands Province & Central Province.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The purpose of this role is to oversee grant implementation and operational activities within Morobe, Western Highlands and Central provinces for the UNICEF Smarter and Safer Schools (3 S) project, delivered by World Vision Papua New Guinea
The role is responsible to supports the design, implementation, coordination, and monitoring of the
Smarter, Safer Schools project
, ensuring that schools are safe, inclusive, resilient, and supportive learning environments. The role focuses on integrating
life skills education
,
child protection
,
school safety
, and
risk-informed education planning
to improve education outcomes for children and adolescents.
MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Programme Planning and Implementation
Support the planning, implementation, and scaling of the
Smarter, Safer Schools framework
in line with UNICEF education and child protection strategies.
Coordinate life skills education interventions that promote
safety, resilience, wellbeing, citizenship, and positive behavior
.
Support schools in integrating
school safety, disaster risk reduction (DRR), climate resilience, and child safeguarding
into school plans and practices.
Life Skills and Child-Centered Education
Promote and support
life skills education
(SEL, life competencies, health, safety, digital literacy, citizenship).
Strengthen child participation, student leadership, and peer-led initiatives within schools.
Ensure gender-responsive, inclusive, and disability-sensitive approaches are applied in all activities.
Capacity Building and Technical Support
Provide technical support and training for teachers, school leaders, education officers, and partners on:
Smarter, Safer Schools standards
Life skills education methodologies
Child protection in schools
School safety and preparedness
Develop and adapt training materials, guidelines, and tools consistent with UNICEF frameworks.
Support mentoring and follow-up to ensure quality implementation at school level
Partnerships and Coordination
Work closely with
government counterparts
, schools, communities, NGOs, and development partners.
Support coordination between education, child protection, health, and emergency sectors.
Engage communities, parents, and youth groups to strengthen ownership and sustainability of interventions
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting
Support monitoring of project activities, indicators, and outcomes related to safer and smarter schools.
Collect, analyze, and document lessons learned and good practices.
Contribute to donor reports, progress updates, and knowledge products.
Equity, Safeguarding, and Accountability
Ensure all interventions uphold
Child Safeguarding, PSEA, and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP)
principles.
Promote equity-focused and rights-based approaches, prioritizing the most vulnerable children.
Identify and mitigate risks related to safety, protection, and inclusion in schools.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
University degree in
Education, Social Sciences, Psychology, Child Development, International Development
, or a related field.
At least
2–5 years
experience in education programming, life skills education, child protection, or school safety.
Experience working with schools, teachers, and education authorities.
Experience in UNICEF, UN, NGOs, or development projects is an asset.
Life skills education and social-emotional learning
Safe schools / child-friendly schools concepts
Child protection in education settings
Gender and inclusion in education
Monitoring and reporting
Strong coordination and communication skills
Ability to work with multiple stakeholders
Problem-solving and analytical skills
Cultural sensitivity and teamwork
Ability to work independently in field-based settings
A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunity will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.
Interested applicants should submit the following documents all in one PDF file before;
Monday 10 August, 2026
,
(Midnight, PNG Time)
Expression of interest
Detailed CV
World Vision is committed to the principles of workplace diversity. Qualified women and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.
World Vision is committed to safeguarding all children and adults living where World Vision operates. We enforce a zero tolerance policy for any forms of violence, abuse and exploitation against children or adults, either by employees or others affiliated with our work. We do not employ staff whose background is not aligned with our safe guarding practices. Employment is conditional upon successful completion of all mandatory background checks, including criminal record checks, where required.
We appreciate the time it takes to prepare your application. Please note that only short-listed candidates suitable for interviews will be contacted. If you do not hear from World Vision within
two (2) weeks
of the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful.
Apply

27916.description:
Goodman Fielder Papua New Guinea is one of PNG’s largest food companies, manufacturing and distributing high quality Flour, Rice, Stock Feed, Snacks and Bakery products throughout the country. The company owns a host of iconic brands which include; Flame Flour, Flame Stockfeed, Bilas Bread, Arthur’s Pie, Twisties, Skel Rice and the Meadow Lea range.
At GFI, we care about making everyday food better for everyone.
Our goal is to be the leading and most innovative local food company with a mission to meet our customers’ needs for superior quality foods with brands that are trusted by families everywhere.  We are the go-to source of consumer, shopper, and customer insights to help our customer and business partners succeed.
We currently have an immediate vacancy for a
Filling Machine Operator
to join our already strong and vibrant Operations team in our
Oil Bottling Plant
in
Lae
. The position oversees the oil filling machine for the setup, changeovers, cleaning and lubrication and operating/monitoring the product filling process.
RESPONSILBILITIES:
Be on time for shift pre-start checks and ensure machine is in correct setup and operating mode.
Operate, monitor and report any failures and defects deterring equipment from normal operation with risks of break down.
Carry out operational adjustments for effective filling process.
Log all necessary information relating to equipment performance including breakdown stopagges.
Support engineering team with repairs and preventative maintenance tasks.
Minimise double work and waste of resources.
Execute daily and weekly cleaning procedures.
Maintain high level of personal hygiene and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
Perform other tasks as directed by the supervisor.
KEY COMPETENCIES / EXPERIENCE:
Technical/Functional Competencies
High Literacy and Numeracy Level
Understanding Food Safety Principles
Technical capability to troubleshoot failures
Leadership Competencies
Excellent Communication
Able to think strategically
Excellent Time Management
Empower and support team (Knowledge sharing)
Experience/ Qualification Required
Minimum Grade 12 Level
PETT/ TVET Training would be an advantage
Minimum of 2 years’ experience working in Food Manufacturing as a Filler Operator
Be part of the Skel life and join a team that values healthy eating and active lifestyles and wants to share that with all the people of PNG. Send your EOI & CV in 1 PDF file to :
The Recruitment Team
Goodman Fielder Papua New Guinea
P O. Box 673, Port Moresby NCD PNG
E-mail:
[email protected]
In the subject line address as
"Filling Machine Operator”
Applications close
Monday 10th August, 2026.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
Apply

27914.description:
Operating in Papua New Guinea for over 30 years, Nestlé PNG Limited is seeking a qualified and
experienced
Electrician
to join our Engineering Team, based at the Lae Factory
Reporting directly to the Electrical Supervisor, the position holder is responsible for safely executing electrical maintenance, troubleshooting, repairs, installations, and preventive maintenance activities across factory equipment and automation systems to ensure reliable manufacturing operations, equipment availability, safety compliance, and continuous improvement within the Nestlé PNG Lae Factory
Key responsibilities:
Perform electrical maintenance, repairs, replacements, and installations of motors, sensors, actuators,
transformers, controllers, circuit breakers, switches, wiring, and other electrical equipment
Troubleshoot, repair, and maintain PLCs, Servo Drives, Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs), and
associated electrical controls and automation systems
Diagnose equipment faults and carry out corrective maintenance using appropriate testing equipment
and electrical drawings
Read and interpret blueprints, wiring diagrams, and schematics to plan and execute electrical work
Perform routine preventive maintenance activities in accordance with maintenance schedules and
factory standards
Support installation, commissioning, and optimization of production and packaging equipment.
Maintain accurate maintenance records and update Nestlé maintenance systems as required.
Ensure compliance with electrical safety requirements, Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures, GMP, and
site safety standards
Maintain high housekeeping and sanitation standards within the work area.
Provide technical support and on-the-job training to production teams and fellow technicians,
contributing to a culture of continuous improvement.
Qualification, skills, and experience:
Electrical Trade Qualification, with Current NEA Electrical Licence preferred
Minimum three (3) years' experience in industrial electrical maintenance, or FMCG operations
Hands-on experience with PLC systems, Servo Drives, Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs), industrial
sensors, and motor control systems
Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, schematics, and technical manuals.
Experience with preventive maintenance systems and troubleshooting industrial equipment.
Sound knowledge of industrial electrical systems, automation equipment, electrical safety procedures,
and Lockout/Tagout practices
Knowledge of GMP, food safety requirements, and continuous improvement principles is desirable.
Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with a high attention to detail
Good communication skills, strong safety awareness, and the ability to work independently and as part
of a team.
At Nestlé, we value diversity, innovation, and a commitment to sustainability. We offer competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and opportunities for personal and professional growth.
If interested, please apply by email to:
[email protected]
Submission closes on Wednesday, 10th August 2026.
Apply

27913.description:
Operating in Papua New Guinea for over 30 years, Nestlé PNG Limited is seeking a qualified and
experienced
Microbiologist
to join our Quality Assurance Team, based at the Lae Factory.
Reporting directly to the Quality Assurance Manager, the position holder is responsible for conducting
microbiological testing, pathogen monitoring, laboratory compliance, Good Laboratory Practices (GLP)
implementation, ISO 17025 documentation, and food safety verification activities to ensure Nestlé products meetmicrobiological safety standards, regulatory requirements, and consumer expectations.
Key responsibilities:
Conduct routine microbiological and pathogen analyses, including Salmonella testing, in accordance
with laboratory procedures and standards.
Register and prepare samples for testing, ensuring accurate documentation and sample traceability.
Prepare microbiological media and maintain adequate stock levels of laboratory chemicals,
consumables, and testing supplies.
Monitor and maintain laboratory records and documentation in compliance with ISO 17025 and Good
Laboratory Practices (GLP).
Participate in proficiency testing programs and ensure analytical results are within acceptable
performance standards.
Support laboratory audits, GLP/5S assessments, and follow-up on corrective actions.
Maintain internal control plans and ensure proper sample retention, labeling, and disposal processes.
Ensure laboratory safety, biosafety requirements, and housekeeping standards are consistently upheld.
Provide technical support and training team members on laboratory standards, GLP, and 5S practices.
Liaise with internal and external stakeholders on sample analysis requests and laboratory services.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that enhance laboratory efficiency, compliance, and
food safety performance.
Qualification, skills, and experience:
Degree in Biological Sciences, Food Science, Applied Science, or a related scientific discipline.
Experience in microbiological testing, food safety labs, pathogen detection, and laboratory operations.
Sound understanding of Good Laboratory Practices (GLP), ISO 17025 requirements, laboratory
documentation, and microbiological testing methods.
Knowledge of food microbiology, pathogen detection techniques, environmental monitoring, and
laboratory safety systems.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a high level of attention to detail.
Excellent organizational and documentation skills.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively across teams.
Ability to work independently while maintaining a strong focus on quality, food safety, and compliance.
Proficiency in MS Office applications and laboratory record management systems will be an advantage.
At Nestlé, we value diversity, innovation, and a commitment to sustainability. We offer competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and opportunities for personal and professional growth.
If interested, please apply by email to:
[email protected]
Submission closes on Wednesday, 10th August 2026.
Apply

27907.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an Advisor People, Training (Trade Trainer – Electrical), you will play a pivotal role in shaping the next generation of skilled electrical tradespeople. By delivering high-quality training, coaching, and assessment, you will help apprentices build the technical expertise, confidence, and safe work practices required to achieve trade competency and successfully complete their apprenticeship journey. Your work will directly contribute to workforce capability, operational excellence, and the long-term success of our business.
As part of our team, you will
Deliver engaging classroom, workshop, field-based, and on-the-job electrical training programs for apprentices.
Coach, mentor, and support apprentices through all stages of their training and development journey.
Monitor apprentice progress, assess competencies, and provide meaningful feedback to support successful outcomes.
Develop and maintain training resources, assessment tools, and learning materials that align with industry requirements and emerging technologies.
Promote a strong safety culture by embedding critical risk controls and safe electrical work practices into every aspect of training delivery.
Partner with operational leaders, maintenance teams, safety professionals, and external training bodies to drive capability development and trade excellence.
Contribute to workforce development initiatives, trade testing programs, and continuous improvement opportunities across the training function
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To thrive in this position, you will bring:
A strong background in electrical trades within mining, oil & gas, heavy industry, or vocational training environments.
Demonstrated experience delivering electrical training, trade testing, apprenticeship programs, or workforce capability initiatives.
A recognised Electrical Trade Qualification and a current PNG Electrical Licence or equivalent.
Certificate IV in Training and Assessment (or equivalent vocational education and training qualification).
Sound knowledge of electrical safety standards, competency-based training, and adult learning principles.
Strong facilitation, coaching, mentoring, and communication skills, with the ability to engage learners at varying stages of development.
A collaborative, adaptable, and solutions-focused approach, with the ability to think creatively and help apprentices achieve their full potential.
Your work environment
You will join a supportive and collaborative training team where capability development, safety, and continuous improvement are highly valued. Working closely with the Team Lead, fellow Trade Trainers, Safety Trainers, operational leaders, and external stakeholders, you will have the opportunity to make a lasting impact on apprentice development while contributing to strategic workforce capability initiatives.
This role offers genuine professional development opportunities, including support for trainer accreditation and ongoing learning aligned with your career as an electrical trade training professional. You'll experience the rewarding challenge of helping apprentices achieve key milestones, develop their careers, and ultimately become qualified tradespeople.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​
Learn more about our purpose and values:
About Newmont
​
Hear from our people:
Life at Newmont
​

.

27709.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As the Technician Core Shed, you will support exploration activities by executing core shed tasks in line with site procedures, exploration standards and operational requirements.
This role will see you carry out core handling, cutting, sampling, geotechnical logging support, data collection and sample management activities. You will play an important role in maintaining accurate geological records, supporting core sample accessibility, and helping ensure core shed processes are completed safely, consistently and in accordance with SOPs.
As part of our team, you will
•    Implement core handling, cutting, sampling and geotechnical logging procedures in line with SOPs.
•    Gather geological data accurately and consistently to support exploration activities.
•    Administer, store and retrieve core samples according to approved procedures.
•    Follow geoscientist instructions for core sampling and related core shed activities.
•    Photograph core samples using standardised processes to maintain consistency and quality.
•    Support the archiving of core photographs in a searchable database linked to geological logs.
•    Follow procedures for core disposal, and core shed operations to help prevent environmental degradation.
•    Support access to archived core for research and analysis by internal teams, external partners or academic institutions.
•    Maintain core storage areas to allow safe, accurate and easy retrieval of samples.
•    Collect XRF, hyperspectral, density and other rock property data from core and chips in line with SOPs.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
•    Practical experience in core handling, sampling, geotechnical logging support or geological data collection.
•    Ability to follow SOPs, site procedures and standardised work processes accurately.
•    Familiarity with core cataloguing, storage and retrieval processes.
•    Experience handling geological samples and maintaining accurate sample records.
•    Ability to support data collection activities, including XRF, hyperspectral, density or other rock property data.
•    Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining quality, consistency and traceability of core shed records.
•    Ability to work safely around exploration equipment, core samples and core shed infrastructure.
•    Strong communication skills, with the ability to ask questions, clarify tasks and follow technical instructions.
•    Ability to work collaboratively with geologists, exploration supervisors, drill supervisors, field logistics team, health and safety teams, laboratory partners and suppliers.
•    Commitment to stopping unsafe work and speaking up when risks or issues are identified.
Desirable experience includes previous experience in a core shed, exploration, geology, mining or field-based technical environment, familiarity with exploration SOPs and guidelines, and experience using Microsoft Office applications such as Excel for data management and Word for documentation.
Your work environment
This is a full-time FIFO role based at Lihir Gold Limited in Papua New Guinea, working on a 21 days on / 21 days off roster. You will support the Technical team within the Sciences and Exploration discipline, working with core samples, exploration data, site SOPs and equipment that supports exploration programs.
You will be part of a team focused on safe core shed operations, accurate sample handling, consistent geological data capture and reliable support for exploration activities across the Lihir operation.
Working Conditions
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.

To maintain and repair fixed plant equipment onsite in a safe, responsible and timely and effective manner ensuring all Fixed Plant and K92 mining standards are met. The Plant Fitter is responsible to maintain all plant equipment and ensure all planning and scheduling maintenance activities are performed safely and more effectively.

Key accountabilities of this position include.
Maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
The successful completion of daily work to meet quality standards and deadlines.
Reporting faults and Hazards and respond to routine emergency calls for repair and service within the mine site area.

Organizational skills including ability to prioritize and manage time.
Good interpersonal and communication skills and perform roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core valves.
Monitoring and assessment of plant and equipment.
Exercise due care and attention to work in a safe and efficient manner.
Completion of daily time sheet with the correct job numbers and time.
Assist in supervising and on-job training for Apprentices and Trade Assistance.
Willingness to assist other trades as and when required.
Work long odd hours and often be on call in emergency situations and extreme conditions
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you should have;
At least 5 years of progressively responsible experience is required.
Graduated from a recognized Tertiary institutions or technical training program in a maintenance trade or completion of a recognized apprenticeship program, or combination of the two.
Trade Certificate Fitting & Machinery / Mechanical Fitting.
Sound knowledge of all Gold Processing Plant Equipment or similar set up.
Ability to trouble shoots and perform root cause analysis (particularly in diagnosis and fault finding).
Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is maintained and the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.
Good working knowledge of the principles and practices of OH&S and Fixed Plant.
Be flexible and adaptable to the needs of the business and ability to work harmoniously as part of the team.

Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
The Superintendent – Surface Workshop is responsible for leading and managing all maintenance activities within the Kumian Surface Workshop facility.
The Superintendent – Surface Workshop will ensure proper upkeep of mobile equipment and fixed infrastructure by overseeing a team of multi-disciplined technicians, developing preventative maintenance programs, adhering to safety regulations, and optimizing maintenance schedules through data analysis, with the objective to minimise downtime and maximise asset life.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Planning & Organising Maintenance
Liaise with the Maintenance Planners to develop and implement comprehensive preventive maintenance schedules.
Prioritise maintenance tasks based on urgency and asset criticality.
Create and manage maintenance budgets.
Allocate resources effectively to maintenance activities.
Team Leadership and Supervision
Recruit, train, and manage a team of maintenance technicians (LV Mechanics, Auto-Electricians, Heavy Equipment Fitters, Panel Beaters, Boilermaker/Welders, Tyre Fitters).
Assign tasks and delegate responsibilities to maintenance team.
Conduct performance evaluations and provide feedback to team members.
Promote a culture of safety and quality within the maintenance team through the K92 Cares program.
Maintenance Operations
Respond to maintenance breakdowns and other repair requests, promptly.
Conduct regular inspections of facilities and equipment to identify potential issues.
Coordinate repairs and upgrades with external contractors when necessary.
Monitor equipment performance and identify areas for improvement.
Reporting and Data Analysis
Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, including Work Orders and repair history.
Generate reports on maintenance costs, performance, and asset availability/utilisation.
Utilise data analysis to identify trends and optimise maintenance strategies.
Communication and Collaboration
Communicate maintenance schedules, updates, and issues to all K92 stakeholders.
Collaborate with other K92 Departments to address maintenance needs and improve service delivery.
Coordinate the management of planned maintenance projects.
Key Goals of the Maintenance Superintendent
Minimise equipment downtime and maximise operational efficiency.
Extend the lifespan of assets through proactive maintenance practices.
Optimise maintenance costs by identifying cost-saving opportunities.
Ensure a safe working environment for maintenance employees and contractors.
Maintain compliance with all relevant safety and regulatory standards.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you should have;
Mechanical Trade certificate.
Current PNG driver’s license
Certificate IV Training & Assessment
Certificate in Frontline Management
Minimum 5 years in Maintenance Supervisory role.
Demonstrated use of industry standard ERP (Oracle, SAP, Pronto) – Maintenance module.
Good level of English literacy – spoken and written.
Competent in the use of MS Office suite (MS Word, MS Excel, and MS Power Point).
Familiarity/experience with Pronto ERP – Maintenance module.
Project Management experience – coordinating small projects.
Mining industry experience.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

27625.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
Implementation of the complete mine power supply and distribution system; and a maintenance system for all electrical equipment in the underground mine and our exploration sites in Kainantu. Training of T/A Electrician to effectively monitor and maintain the electrical systems in the mine, with particular reference to the electrical components.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Diagnose electrical defects or hazards on systems, appliances and machinery and identify adjustment and repair timely.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment, appliances, and machines.
Inspect, test and qualified to apply and remove ‘out-of-service’ or ‘not-to-be operated’ tags to electrical equipment, appliances, and machines.
Prepare sketches and plan layout to determine the location of electrical wiring and equipment and to always ensure safety compliance.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment, and machines.
Delegate routine tasks to subordinates and provide supervision where required.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair and service within the mine site area, underground and on field, or where job is required.
Work long and odd hours and often be on call in emergency situations and extreme conditions.
Attend to physically demanding tasks involving digging ditches and moving and lifting heavy objects.
Perform general housekeeping within and around work area.
Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
Ensure that the sections daily work plans are executed as directed.
Competent in lifting and safe operation of workshop equipment.
Reading and understanding technical drawings and manuals.
Diagnose problems in all equipment with regular reference to equipment manuals.
Prepare and plan of welding jobs for site services.
Carry out equipment alignments with Dial Indicators.
Conduct accurate dimensional checks of crusher bushes, shafts or bearing clearances and recording data.
Attend to isolations required for simple tasks to major shutdowns.
Conduct general housekeeping at work area.
Identify and report safety hazards.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
To be considered for this role, you should have;
Grades 10 or 12 certificate
Must be a NATTB Level 3 Electrical Mechanic Tradesman with PNG Power EW10 certification.
Maintain current NEA electrician’s license to meet government regulations.
Wide experience in the installation and maintenance of underground power distribution systems, transformer installations, motor control centres, LVHV transfers, and starters; and in the maintenance of underground equipment – electric motors, compressor stations and other electrical equipment.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

Company Overview
MTIS Group is a highly equipped, specialized company providing engineering, commissioning, maintenance, procurement, and sales solutions across all major industrial sectors. With a core focus on integrity, communication, and cost reduction without compromising quality of service, we are dedicated to setting the standard in quality and support across our multidisciplinary range of services and products. Our main headquarters, service, and production facility is located in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea.

We are seeking a skilled and safety-focused Pipe Fitter to join our Projects and Engineering Department at our Motukea facility. Reporting to the Lead Fabrication Supervisor or Project Manager, this hands-on workshop Pipe Fitter role is responsible for  the assembly, installation, maintenance , and repair of piping system .

Read and interpret isometric drawings, P&IDs, and technical specifications

Knowledge of industry standards and codes.

High Attention to details and precision.

27887.description:
SPECTRA POM IS HIRING
– 2X MECHANICS
!
Spectra Industrial Limited - a Leader in Sales, Service and Hire of Forklifts, Gensets and Industrial Supplies, is seeking two (2) organized, qualified, and well experienced Mechanics to join our POM Workshop Team and be a part of our growing enterprise!
Position Description
Position Title: Mechanic (2 Positions)
Company: Spectra Industrial Limited
Location: Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Reports To: Operations Manager / Southern Region Manager
Position Purpose
Mechanics will be responsible for inspecting, servicing, diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining company vehicles, forklifts, gensets, plant, and equipment to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operation. Applicants must hold a recognized mechanical trade qualification and a current PNG driver’s license, with practical workshop experience, strong safety awareness, and the ability to complete maintenance records accurately.
Key Responsibilities
Inspection, Servicing & Preventive Maintenance
Carry out routine inspections, servicing, lubrication, and preventive maintenance on vehicles, plant, and equipment.
Perform pre-start, scheduled, and breakdown maintenance in line with workshop procedures and client standards.
Identify worn or damaged parts and recommend timely repair or replacement.
Fault Diagnosis & Repairs
Diagnose mechanical faults on engines, driveline, brakes, steering, suspension, and basic electrical systems.
Repair, overhaul, or replace defective parts and components using correct tools and workshop practices.
Test equipment after repair to confirm safe and reliable operating condition.
Workshop Tools, Parts & Equipment Care
Use workshop tools, testing equipment, and manuals correctly and safely.
Maintain tools and workshop equipment in good condition and report defects promptly.
Assist with ordering, collection, and proper use of spare parts, lubricants, and consumables.
Safety, Compliance & Housekeeping
Comply with company safety procedures, PPE requirements, toolbox talks, and Papua New Guinea workplace safety standards.
Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free workshop and work area.
Report hazards, incidents, unsafe equipment, and non-conformances promptly to the supervisor.
Documentation & Reporting
Complete job cards, service reports, inspection checklists, and maintenance records accurately and on time.
Record parts used, work completed, and outstanding repairs clearly for workshop tracking.
Communicate equipment status, defects, and maintenance priorities to supervisors and relevant teams.
Teamwork & Operational Support
Work closely with drivers, operators, stores, and workshop staff to meet operational requirements.
Assist apprentices or junior staff with on-the-job guidance where required.
Undertake additional duties, training, or site support as reasonably directed by management.
Breakdown & Field Support
Respond to workshop or field breakdowns and carry out repairs efficiently to minimize downtime.
Support site-based maintenance activities where travel or roster work is required.
Ensure repaired vehicles and equipment are safe, roadworthy, and ready for operation.
Key Competencies & Skills
Mechanical aptitude and diagnostic ability.
Safety awareness and compliance.
Attention to detail and workmanship.
Communication and reporting skills.
Teamwork, reliability, and initiative.
Ability to work under pressure and meet operational deadlines.
Qualifications & Experience
Minimum Grade 10 education, Grade 12 is an advantage.
Recognized Mechanical Tradesman Certificate in Automotive, Motor Vehicle Mechanics, Diesel Fitting, Heavy Equipment, or related mechanical trade from a recognized institution; NATTB-certified trade qualification is highly preferred.
Minimum 3–5 years’ relevant mechanic experience in a workshop, fleet, plant, construction, mining, oil and gas, or industrial environment.
Sound knowledge of preventive maintenance, fault diagnosis, repair procedures, and safe work practices.
Experience working on light vehicles, diesel equipment, plant, or heavy equipment is highly desirable.
Current and valid PNG driver’s license is required – Class 6 or relevant license for light/heavy vehicles will be an added advantage.
Ability to read service manuals, complete workshop documentation, and work independently or as part of a team.
Interested in joining our Competitive, Responsive and Committed Team?
Send your updated resumes with contactable referees, trade certificate, driver’s license copy, and relevant supporting documents, to email:
[email protected]
with “Mechanic – POM” on the subject line.
Applications can also be hand delivered to our Port Moresby branch Office.
Attention: HR Recruitment Team
Spectra Industrial Ltd
P.O. Box 7528
Boroko, NCD
Remuneration will be discussed during the interview.
For all positions we require current and verifiable workplace referees to be provided. Any references and qualifications provided will be verified and checked should your application get to shortlist stage.
Note:
Applications are open to PNG citizens only.
Priority will be given to the POM based applicants.
Former applicants need not re-apply.
Female applicants are encouraged to apply.
Application closes on COB Friday 07
